task.description:

**Milestone:** M5
**Stable plan reference:** RSF-v1.1/M5-02
**Implementation status:** Implemented and independently verified for bounded RSF-24 scope; final acceptance recorded in the authoritative Kaneo column.
**Responsible implementer:** Codex (aM3as9DCoQ7pMoO3V9XsDbL3q2j9pWjn). Independent read-only reviewer: /root/rsf24_qa; ownership remains with Codex.
**Source reference:** docs/architecture/RO_SPRITE_FORGE_COMPREHENSIVE_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN_v1.1.md §§4.5–4.6, 6/M5, 9
**Planning source SHA-256:** 5edfbebcdb47620c59a915e8874094f35092125dd0444b79468aa55a191a361e

## Problem and expected outcome

**Objective:** Keep ACT pool/index references correct across reuse and explicit conversion.

**Scope:** Stored/referenced image identity, dedup/reuse ordering, indexed preserve path and explicit RGBA SPR 2.1 conversion.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Fix pool/image ordering and identity/reuse policy deterministically; ACT references resolve to the intended image in mixed-pool outputs.
- [x] Keep unchanged indexed original path byte-preserving; RGBA conversion requires opt-in and palette/index-information loss report.
- [x] Explicit conversion verifies decoded pixels and remapped references independently; preview RGBA never silently dictates output representation.
- [x] Reject missing references, invalid pool/index values and unsupported conversions with exact occurrence diagnostics.

## Verification

Synthetic mixed-pool/reuse/duplicate-content/unused-image and conversion negative tests; Rust decoded reference/pixel checks.

Actual commands, environment, exit statuses, artifact hashes and exclusions are recorded in docs/verification/rsf-24/VERIFICATION.md, implementation-manifest.json and QA_REVIEW.md. Native Korangar remains UNVERIFIED.

## Non-goals and dependencies

**Dependencies:** RSF-23 (M5-01; task ID vn81mars8cnptoeyxxi592po)

**Non-goals / gate qualifications:** Only the stated deliverable; no adjacent milestone implementation or automatic artistic/native acceptance.

Original Ragnarok artwork/GRFs and private fixtures stay outside public Git/deliverables. Use synthetic redistributable fixtures for public verification. Private fixture/tool availability must be checked during execution, never assumed.

## Implementation evidence (add at QA handoff)

- Code/diff: docs/verification/rsf-24/implementation.diff; 10 narrowly changed implementation/test files. Existing ACT/SPR codecs and Rust source unchanged.
- Implementation manifest SHA-256: c23f28b4fce4191dd9e15dc9c19414c59739226fda8535ca8902f4fea022f859.

Python 3.14.4/Pillow 12.1.1. Python 3.12/3.13 unavailable NOT_RUN.
- Golden outputs: ACT 2ac52f933b5f78cdc1959ceb20c1b7be34e8c6ea92f42d21c1d70b1d71de1778; SPR ea072d9946582629e3e721ad30d973a71366c609dab080cf23ea08110bf7ee40; canonical compilation 381f0b70c493d7be90f784ddd7a18aadcdd55c35b4da2ded9041fe8386cd990f.
- M5-S PASS for this bounded structural/preservation task; M5-I PASS; M5-N UNVERIFIED. M5 remains open. No subjective artwork approval, production readiness or new native playback claimed.

**Responsible implementer:** Unassigned. Required skill: Authorized engineer for this bounded deliverable; independent reviewer is separate.
**Source reference:** docs/architecture/RO_SPRITE_FORGE_COMPREHENSIVE_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN_v1.1.md §§2.3, 4.3–4.6, 6/M5, 8, 12
**Planning source SHA-256:** 5edfbebcdb47620c59a915e8874094f35092125dd0444b79468aa55a191a361e

## Problem and expected outcome

**Objective:** Publish repeatable builds from approved canonical inputs without false production labels.

**Scope:** Canonical ordering/numerics/encoders, build identity/manifest, cache, atomic publication and production/diagnostic gates.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Same source/contract/profile/composition/toolchain/output policy in two clean builds at different paths/times yields identical SPR/ACT SHA-256 hashes.
- [ ] Specify schema/action/view/frame/layer/image ordering and numeric rounding/field encodings; pin decoder/resampler/palette/color-space/encoder versions. Never reorder semantically ordered layers.
- [ ] Build identity excludes timestamps, hostname, absolute paths, random UUIDs, filesystem traversal order and native-test data; linked verification evidence remains outside deterministic artifact inputs.
- [ ] Production export rejects underspecified/missing/invalid/stale or unapproved required assignments; partial diagnostic exports are conspicuously PARTIAL_DIAGNOSTIC with scoped/full states separate.
- [ ] Manifest includes source/target/profile/policy/tool hashes, approved pre-build composition digest, output hashes and preservation/conversion policy; atomic cache/publication cannot mutate originals or publish partial production output.

## Verification

Two-clean-build hash equality, ordering/rounding regressions, interrupted publication, fail-closed export and changed-one-source affected-approval checks.

Record actual commands, environment/tool versions, exit statuses, artifact hashes and NOT_RUN blockers at handoff. No tests, approvals or native runs are claimed by this planning record.

## Non-goals and dependencies

**Dependencies:** RSF-24 (M5-02; task ID nw62kniena0oeqe44yba8uil)

**Non-goals / gate qualifications:** Build/native evidence never creates aesthetic approval.

Original Ragnarok artwork/GRFs and private fixtures stay outside public Git/deliverables. Use synthetic redistributable fixtures for public verification. Private fixture/tool availability must be checked during execution, never assumed.

## Implementation evidence (add at QA handoff)

- Code changes / diff: Not implemented by this planning sync.
- Test commands / exit statuses / artifact hashes: NOT_RUN (planning only).
- Milestone gates / limitations: Not evaluated; structural, coverage, visual, preview and native states remain separate.

## Independent QA result (reviewer reports, coordinator syncs)

Not performed for implementation. Implementer supplies evidence and moves to QA Review; a distinct read-only reviewer records QA_PASS / QA_FAIL / QA_BLOCKED. Operator-only visual/native decisions remain separate. No acceptance is granted by backlog creation.
